title: Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier: three made pieces that each walk up to a test the page's own text sets (the boil meter read where nothing moves, a paper grain fixed or carried, and the exact place a warp folds), with BLUELINE's own loops, boards and M3.7 pair gathered beside the sections they prove, the fingerprint of the words each was laid against, and the offers the pieces measured for the text. I grow when a piece has something new to test; I never hold the entry's words.
entry: Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It

offers.what: The 0.15/255 was never a warp's number. The bench measured it on its NPR stylizer run over a Blender smoke sim (track-VI report.md:85, Tier C), against per-frame SDXL img2img on the same sim; the warp was measured only for its loop seam (0.0). Read with the same meter (stylize.py's flicker: mean |frame − frame before| × 255) on the bench's own warp loops, which cannot boil: smoke 0.86, sky 1.79, water 1.98, dust 4.77, flame 8.72 (mp4 previews in report-assets; the piece's own smoke loop reads 0.64). The meter counts motion and boil together, so a warp scores whatever its motion is. Proposed first bullet: "deterministic NPR on one fixed grain — 0.15 / 255, all of it the sim's own motion", and a line that the warp's boil is zero by construction, which the piece shows as exactly 0 where nothing moves.

"~10× worse, and that figure flatters the AI" runs the wrong way. The bench's debrief (debrief.html:189) gives the reason: the AI run "sampled sparse frames with more real motion between them", and more motion per pair raises the AI's number, so it overstates the AI's boil rather than flattering it. Measured on the NPR clip read k frames apart: 0.12 (1), 0.24 (2), 0.45 (4), 0.84 (8), 1.41 (15). Part of the 1.50 is motion; how much can't be re-measured, because renders/smoke_ai_flick is gitignored and not on this Mac. On the mp4 preview the 0.15 itself reads 0.12 within the 90-frame sim and 0.16 counting the restart jump. Proposed: "per-frame AI restyle — 1.50 / 255, read on sparser frames, so part of it is motion. Boil is the change where nothing moved, and you see it before you can read it."

offers.section: The same rule, the substrate too
offers.what: "A static substrate cannot boil" holds: on the piece's port of stylize.py (npr_ink matches to 1.5e-7, the blur to scipy's to 6e-8), a grain made once reads exactly 0 on plain paper where nothing moves, a fresh grain each frame 0.63. But a static grain can slide: it stays on the screen while the ink moves through it, the shower-door effect (Meier, Painterly Rendering for Animation, SIGGRAPH 1996). Measured after following the motion: 8.77/255 with the grain fixed, 0.33 with the grain carried by the same motion. Carrying it is inking once and warping, so it needs a displacement; a billowing sim has none, and the slide is the fixed grain's cost there. Proposed after "A static substrate cannot boil." (the challenger's wording): "It can slide, though: on a sim, the grain stays on the screen while the smoke moves through it. A warp pays no such cost; there the grain is in the still and moves with the ink."

The warp's own edge is det J > 0 along the path: it rearranges the ink only while det J of the source map x − d(x) never reaches zero as the push grows (for one ripple of length λ, a push under λ/2π). The sign at the end is not enough: past the fold a ripple can fold on both axes and read positive again (the piece marks those; dust at default push folds on 1 pixel that way). On the piece's engine the drawing keeps 4 islands and 1 hole over 480 frames up to 0.95 of the fold, and at 1.4 shows 4 to 8 islands and 1 to 4 holes as mirrored creases. Measured on fields.py: at default push sky's tightest det J 0.90, dust 0.05, water 0.02, smoke 0.01, flame −0.07 (318 px); as the bench rendered its loops, where experiments.html records it, water_v1 at amp 1.3 folds on up to 3,605 px (det J −0.27) and flame_v1 on a full mask on up to 936 (−0.20). Those loops read as water and flame and no one saw a crease. Proposed, after the first paragraph: "The warp has an edge of its own: it rearranges the ink only while it never folds back on itself (det J stays above 0 as the push grows; for a ripple of length λ, a push under λ/2π). The bench crossed it on a few thousand pixels without a visible crease, so the visible edge comes later than the mathematical one, and the edge that matters is still a shape the still never drew."

In the M3 rhyme the word "warp" changes sides. What lost in M3.7 was warping the diffusion noise one step along the motion while the model still redrew every frame (adjacent embedding coherence 0.858 seed-lock vs 0.809 warped, m3.7-report.md); here the warp is what wins. The lesson is the same, but read beside this page, "a locked seed beat per-step warp" can sound like the opposite. Proposed: "a locked seed beat per-step warping of the noise".

verdicts.why: A real test, numbers rerun (seam 0 and 7.97; boil 4.26 flat, motion 0.88/3.20/8.52), but step 5 states 'boil does not grow with the gap' as general when it holds by construction for a twin with fresh nudges, and the twin's 4.3 is set by its slider (almost 3x the AI's whole 1.50). Scope that verdict to the twin, say the twin's scale is arbitrary, and say 'boil, moved' reads 0 because that region is where the field is zero.
The only record of the AI frames, captioned honestly. Note: the board's own NPR label 'draw once, move ink' is where the page's warp/NPR merge came from.

pieces.file: Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It — rich — move it or redraw it.html
pieces.title: move it, or redraw it · five steps
pieces.caption: **Move it, or redraw it.** The bench's inked smoke plate, one still, pushed by the bench's own smoke field (fields.py, seed 3, ported and matched to 2e-6 px), then the loop closed: frame 60 against frame 0 reads exactly 0 with whole turns, 7.97/255 with a turn and a half, where the field ends exactly reversed. Then a twin redrawn every frame (a stand-in made here: each mark re-placed by a fresh nudge, not an image model), with the meter split into change where the field moves the ink and change where nothing moves. The test: the moved loop reads exactly 0 where nothing moves (that is where the field is zero); read further apart, motion grows (0.88, 3.20, 8.52 at 1, 4, 15 frames) while the twin's boil holds (4.26, 4.33, 4.28), because each of its redraws is fresh. The twin's boil is set by its nudge slider and says nothing about the AI's 1.50. Then the page's numbers on the bench's clips: the 0.15 is the NPR stylizer on a sim, the 1.50 was read on sparser frames, and the warp loops, which cannot boil, read 0.86 to 8.72. Checked in Node on the piece's own engine.

pieces.file: Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It — rich — one grain.html
pieces.title: one grain · five steps
pieces.caption: **One grain.** stylize.py's paper tooth and NPR ink, ported (npr_ink matched to 1.5e-7), on a swaying puff of smoke: the grain alone, one still inked on it, a fresh grain each frame (boil 0.63 on plain paper where nothing moves), one grain made once (boil exactly 0, the page's claim). The test is the moving edge: a grain fixed to the screen slides under the ink, 8.77/255 after following the motion, the shower-door effect; carried with the puff it reads 0.33, and carrying it is the page's own rule again, ink once and move. Checked in Node on the piece's own engine.

verdicts.file: Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It — rich — where the warp folds.html
verdicts.why: A real test (sweep 480 frames, 4·1 only; λ/2π derivation right). But det J > 0 at the end is not enough for a separable ripple: both factors can go negative and the red overlay misses it (the table's own dust row folds at det +0.05). And the table is at default push while the bench's loops were pushed harder (water at 1.3 folds on 3,605 px). Say both in the hint and the equation note.
Caption matches the board and report-phys-motion.md (anaglyph, block-matching flow; velocity p99 33.8 px vs 98.4 procedural).

pieces.file: Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It — rich — where the warp folds.html
pieces.title: where the warp folds · five steps
pieces.caption: **Where the warp folds.** One arrow moving one dot of ink, then a ripple over a small drawing (a ring, two blobs, a curl), pushed until the ink smears (det J toward 0) and then past the fold, where the frame reads the still backwards. Folded means det J reached zero on the way up as the push grows, not only below zero at the end: past the fold a ripple can fold on both axes and read positive again. The test counts islands and holes: short of the fold the drawing keeps 4 and 1 at every push and phase (480 frames checked); a billow that wants a puff to break off and a hole to open (5 and 2) is out of reach, and past the fold the count changes only as mirrored creases. Last, BLUELINE's fields at default push (sky's tightest det J 0.90, dust 0.05, water 0.02, smoke 0.01, flame −0.07) and two loops as the bench recorded rendering them: water_v1 at × 1.3 folds on up to 3,605 px, flame_v1 on a full mask on up to 936. Nobody saw a crease in either, so the visible edge comes later than the mathematical one. Checked in Node on the piece's engine and in Python on fields.py.
